'''''Koh-Lanta: Bocas del Toro''''' is the third season of ''[[Koh-Lanta]]''.

''Bocas del Toro'' is remembered for its harsh living conditions that led to five [[Evacuation|medical evacuations]] and one [[quit]]. After 40 days, [[Delphine Bano]] and [[Isabelle Seguin]] tied in a 3-3 [[jury]] vote at the [[Final Tribal Council]]. As a result, both were declared [[Sole Survivor|Dual Survivors]]. To date, the season has produced three returning players ([[Tony Sanchez|Antoine Sanchez]], [[Moundir Zoughari]] and [[Moussa Niangane]]) for future seasons.

==Production==
Filmed in 2003, the season took place in the {{wp|Bocas del Toro Province}} in {{wp|Panama}}. The series later returned to Panama for the [[Koh-Lanta: Panama|fourth season]], which was filmed in the {{wp|Pearl Islands}}.

The prize for the winner was €100,000, equivalent to roughly US$109,000 in 2023.

==Twists/Changes==
* '''[[Schoolyard Pick]]:''' The oldest male and female castaways would choose their tribemates in a Schoolyard Pick.
* '''Replacements:''' Due to the high amount of evacuations and quits that took place this season, two castaways returned after their initial elimination, and two new castaways entered midway through the game.
* '''[[Mock Vote]]/[[Exile Island (twist)|Exile Islet]]:''' As the season didn't have enough people to replace all of the evacuations and quits during the season, at the Day 31 Tribal Council, rather than being voted out of the game, the castaway with the most votes would be exiled for 48 hours.
* '''Late [[Merge]]:''' The [[tribe]]s merged when only eight castaways remained.

==Trivia==
* This is the first season in any [[Survivor (franchise)|''Survivor'' franchise]] to feature a tie at the [[Final Tribal Council]]. It would later be followed by ''[[Koh-Lanta: Palawan]]'', ''[[Survivor Philippines: Celebrity Showdown]]'', {{S|36}} and ''[[Koh-Lanta: Le Totem Maudit]]''.
* ''Bocas del Toro'' is the first ''Koh-Lanta'' season to feature a [[quit]].
